That's why you will see the operating cash flow was negative at that time because execution was done but we couldn't convert it into billing at the WIP level.

items.quote: The total receivables is approximately INR 65 crores in 2026, out of which we have billed INR 27 crores in March, which is realizable in the next three months. So, there is no big difference, no very big variance.

items.quote: Yes, as of 31st March. So, 31st March, including all the investments and everything, we have roughly around INR134 crores. items.quote: And coming to the core cash flow from operations, this is our biggest improvement where you will see that it has gone to positive INR12.63 crores for the financial year 2026. This is predominantly because of strong operational performance, better inventory and receivables control.

items.statement: Receivables at INR42.87 crores as of March 31, 2026 with only INR2.31 crores over 180 days and confident of collection with no bad debts expected
items.quote: Coming to our receivable levels, we are at INR42.87 crores for March 31, 2026, out of which only INR2.31 crores is greater than 180 days and we are confident of receiving the same and no chance of growing bad debts.

items.statement: Only remaining related-party transaction with Bang Overseas is fabric supply; other transactions have been transitioned to Thomas Scott and will phase out over time.
items.quote: The only related party transaction that remains with Bang Overseas, which will remain over a period of time, is that they are a fabric supplier to us and we will continue to purchase fabric on a nominal basis from them.

items.statement: Operating cash flow will turn positive only when growth rate aligns with ROCE of 23-25%; currently focused on growth over cash generation.
items.quote: So far as we keep continuing this growth without any further infusion of capital, it is not easy to have positive operating cash flows. So, it is only when the overall opportunity is seized and we start growing at a rate which is similar to our return on capital employed of 23-24% or even 25%. It is during those times that the cash flow from operations would start becoming positive.

items.statement: Receivables have decreased from FY25 to FY26 and will continue to decrease; working capital improvements are ongoing.
items.quote: The receivables have actually come down this year from last year, from FY25 to FY26. And this will continue to decrease further. Because that's what we are working on.

items.statement: Short-term borrowing of Rs. 22 crores is against insurance claim receivable; will decrease once claim is received.
items.quote: Again, about Rs. 22 crores of short-term debt is attributable to an amount that relates to our insurance claim. So, once that is received, then it goes lower to that extent.

items.statement: Other current assets increased to Rs. 46 crores mainly due to Rs. 22 crore insurance claim receivable and Rs. 7-8 crores in deposits with authorities.
items.quote: So, the other current assets comprise of an insurance claim receivable from a previous fire incident that occurred last year to the tune of about 22 crores approximately. That is one part of it. Second part to it, there is also certain deposits that we have, financial deposits, either with the government or certain financial authorities. items.statement: Company holds INR100 crore of own cash, with INR60 crore free cash as of March 2026; customer cash rolls over every 48 hours
items.quote: We have got about INR100 crores of cash in our books, our own cash. Out of the free cash is about INR60 crores as of March '26. In addition to the customer, which is for the CMS business, which gets rolled out within every 48 hours.

items.statement: Collection increased 9% year-on-year to INR421 crores in FY26
items.quote: collection increased by 9% year-on-year to INR421 crores, reflecting sustained customer demand and healthy traction across our portfolio.

items.statement: Balanced receivables of INR2,105 crores from sold and unsold areas of ongoing projects
items.quote: We have balanced receivables of INR2,105 crores from sold and unsold areas of ongoing projects, providing strong cash flow visibility and reinforcing our confidence in the company's long-term growth trajectory.

items.statement: Collection during Q4 FY26 stood at INR112 crores
items.quote: Collection during the quarter stood at INR112 crores.

items.statement: Receivables grew from INR119 crore to INR124 crore in H2 FY26 due to collection issues on four contracts; most cleared in April, bringing debtors down to INR120 crore.

items.statement: Aging shows more than 180 days receivables around INR5 crore; rest mostly within 180 days.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents around INR67.13 crore; other non-current assets around INR16.22 crore; unutilized IPO proceeds INR36.91 crore.
items.quote: If you look at our cash and cash equivalents, it's around INR67.13 crores and other non-current assets is around INR16.22 crores.

items.quote: broadly speaking, for Nykaa, we receive payments in about 2 to 3 months, and sometimes it goes up to 120 days. For Flipkart, we keep our inventory there, so that goes into the inventory account. It is similar for our FOFO stores. Basically, I needed capital because as Recode expands, the FOFO store owners do not have enough capital to always buy from me in cash or give me immediate payment.

items.statement: FOFO stores sold on credit with 2-3 month collection period; inventory given to FOFO recorded as sale but functions like consignment

items.statement: Dead inventory historically around 1%; slow-moving products distributed as goodies in masterclasses before expiry
items.quote: Our historical data shows that dead inventory was around 1%. We do not really have dead inventory. We conduct masterclasses. If we have launched a product that has an expiry of 24 or 36 months, and the product is not moving from the shelves in 6 months or a year, it is likely not going to sell in the following 3 months either. So, we include that product as goodies.

items.statement: Receivables over 6 months increasing due to EPC credit terms and retention money; no bad debt issues
items.quote: Receivables constitute your Chemical as well as your EPC as well as your rentals. So, in overall, like EPC is going on. So, there are some terms and conditions there that we have to extend the credit terms by more than 60 days, 90 days. So that is the reason, one of the reasons.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle peaked at 176 days in Q2 FY26 and is improving sequentially; targeting 120-130 days.
items.quote: Cash conversion cycle had peaked in Q2 to 176 days and has started improving sequentially. This is a major area of focus for us and a major area of de-risking, where we are working on improving both our inventory, receivables and payables days in line with more clear benchmarks.

items.statement: Receivables increased due to warehousing commitments to key OEMs; will stabilize going forward.
items.quote: We have made warehousing or stocking commitments to some customers, where they keep some safety stock and have a more just-in-time delivery. Some of our key OEMs, so that would increase some receivables in the short term. But it will stabilize going forward.

items.statement: Clean audit roadmap moved to Phase 2; hired external consultant to work with statutory and internal auditors on critical observations.
items.quote: Finally, the clean Audit Roadmap has moved to Phase 2. This is a very important governance and compliance initiative, where we are working closely with our statutory auditors and our internal auditors. To work on all their critical observations, in our accounting system, in our controls across various business processes.

items.statement: Phase 2 of clean audit roadmap involves clearing entries, simplifying ledgers in SAP for more robust reporting.
items.quote: This involves a lot of, I would say, going deep inside our SAP data into our books of accounts, doing some clearing entries, simplifying the ledgers and things like that, so that our reporting of numbers becomes much, much more robust, much more seamless and reliable.

items.quote: Pre-tax free cash flow will be positive because if you will see there is an inventory of around INR20 crores at the March, okay. So, it will get sold mostly in the April, okay. So, this cash flow will be -- just a moment. Yes. So, inventory will be positive.

items.statement: Cash and bank balance is less than INR5 crores; company has both long-term and short-term loans but does not intend to raise more equity or debt for growth
items.quote: if I just look at your balance sheet, the cash levels are, I think, it's less than INR5 crores if I'm not wrong, and you have, both I think long-term loans and short-term loans.

items.statement: Loans on asset side of INR13.8 crores comprise advance for property purchase, security deposits, and advances to employees
items.quote: So, it's advance for the property purchase and some is security deposit and some is advance to employees.

items.quote: And the promoter infuses 85 crores in terms of equity. The security that has been given Against this is first charge on the fixed assets and the second charge on current assets and personal and corporate guarantees of the promoters as well as the associate companies and the pledge of shares of promoters.

items.statement: Management expects to replace high-cost NCDs within 15-16 months using internal accruals and improved EBITDA from Project Jagriti and food services growth.

items.statement: Net cash flow from operating activities turned positive at INR4.7 crores versus negative INR1.425 crores in FY25
items.quote: Net cash flow from the operating activities stood at INR4.7 crores positive compared to negative INR1.425 crores in FY2024-25.

items.statement: Operating cash flow expected to turn positive by H1 FY27 after IPO fund deployment into inventory in FY26
items.quote: So, we are likely to get better operating cash flow in this year since that was the last year when we initially deployed our funds into stock s. items.quote: So, because of that reason, because we already supplied and we did not raise our invoices because the commissioning is not happening because our order, most of the time is including the SITC, which 1s supply, installation, testing, and commissioning, all the four sectors

items.quote: Company has approximately raised INR31.39 crores through the IPO proceeding. And most of them are already used for the purpose of which we have raised the money. On a very, very small amount, because of some materials are too rich, that is pending. And that is also going to be utilized very soon, which is maybe 0.5% of the entire amount.

items.statement: XDuce Infotech acquired 25% stake from promoters at market value
items.quote: We had strategically aligned with XDuce Infotech, which is U.S.-based IT service company, and they acquired 25% stake of the company through market value from promoters.

items.statement: UCI New York signed shareholding agreement to acquire 25% stake in UCI
items.quote: UCI have signed recently. This is not in FY26, but this is just last month, we signed a shareholding agreement with UCI New York that they will be acquiring a 25% stake in UCI.

items.statement: Board approved transfer of Talligence and product businesses to Technosys Private Limited for INR11.90 crores cash
items.quote: The Board approved the transfer of Talligence and product businesses to Technosys Private Limited for cash consideration of approximately INR11.90 crores.

items.statement: Continued investing in people through ESOP initiatives
items.quote: Additionally, we continued investing in our people through employee stock ownership, ESOP, initiatives, reinforcing our commitment to attract, retain and reward high-quality talent.

items.statement: Promoter holding around 25%, plan to increase significantly over next 2-3 years
items.quote: There is definitely, yeah, yeah, there is definitely a plan to get it up to a decently significant holding. That is work in progress right now, and the plan over the next 2 years is 2 to 3 years is to make sure that there is a significant increase in the promoter stakeholder.

items.statement: Funding for acquisitions and AI unit came from last year's rights issue proceeds and internal accruals
items.quote: So, the funding came from the rights issue that we did last year. From those , from the proceeds of that and certain accruals, we've been funding all these acquisitions and these future development initiatives.

items.statement: May consider further fundraising in next 2-3 years if funding mismatch arises
items.quote: We are looking at a pipeline for the next two to three years. If there is a mismatch that we would figure out, then we may go into more further fundraise, but nothing at the moment.

items.statement: Cash flow cycles remain long due to milestone-based payments and longer IP revenue cycles; expect improvement after accruals start
items.quote: The content business in terms of payment cycles remains pretty much the same. These are primarily going to be either milestone-based payments or they're going to be credit periods that accrue over a period of time.

items.statement: Other financial assets jumped from INR104 lakhs to INR1,198 lakhs due to unbilled revenue and IP inventory
items.quote: primarily a lot of some of it is unbilled revenue, some of it is certain IPs inventory that we've, you know, we've created which right now would get accrued.

items.statement: Inventory rose to INR 62 crores and operating cash flow stayed negative due to delayed execution from geopolitical situation and rare earth material injunctions by China
items.quote: Inventory rose to about INR 62 crores and the operating cash flow stayed negative again this year, sir.

items.statement: Operating cash flow expected to start improving in FY27 but FY28 would be a better period to judge cash flow
items.quote: FY27, it would start sprouting, but I would be happy to say FY28 would be a better period for us to judge the cash flow.

items.statement: May need capital infusion via debt or other means if taking more API seal orders at subsidized prices
items.quote: if we are going for more API infusion -- API seal infusion, and if we're going to subsidize and take many orders, at that time, we may need capital infusion either by creating debt or by some other means.

items.statement: Trade receivables rose to Rs 205 crore because most sales occurred in March; only 3-5% over 6 months excluding retention
items.quote: Actually, as we have told you, that maximum deliveries of goods were... happened in the month of March because of the issues pertaining through October, when we are talking about H2. So, maximum billing of supply of material happened in the month of March, and you never get money just after the supply.

items.statement: Other current assets of Rs 58 crore represent retention money tied up in government projects
items.quote: So, this other current asset is the retention amount, which is basically tied up with the government projects.

items.statement: Management expects positive operating cash flow in FY27 by selecting projects based on bottom line and cash flows
items.quote: And yes, of course, we see a positive cash flow, because as I told earlier that this, the last year is a learning year for us. And, we have also... I, I had said that now, we will be not focusing only on revenue or top line, rather we'll be selecting the projects based on the bottom line and the cash flows.

items.statement: Promoter family may buy shares in coming months as stock is down over 75%
items.quote: Definitely, you will see in coming months, huh? You might see in coming months.

items.statement: Overseas inventory exceeds INR50 crores as of 31 March 2026 to improve delivery and retail participation
items.quote: The group continues to maintain strategically positioned inventory in excess of INR50 crores as at 31st of March 2026.

items.statement: Cash and bank balance of INR 2,434 lakh at end of FY26 with virtually debt-free balance sheet
items.quote: We ended financial year 2026 with net worth of INR3,751 lakh, cash and bank balance of INR2,434 lakh, and a virtually debt-free balance sheet.

items.statement: Inventory days improved from 150 to 130 days; focused on receivables collection and took client advances against bank guarantees to improve cash flow cycle
items.quote: Our inventory levels improved from 150 days last year to 130 days currently. We have focused more on the collection of receivables and improved our trade payables by providing advances to secure price benefits.

items.statement: Internal goal to reduce inventory days to 90-100 days; using TReDS, bill discounting, LC limits and client advances against bank guarantees to improve working capital
items.quote: We improved from 160 days last year to 130 days in FY25. Our internal goal is 90 to 100 days. However, because we do custom fabrication, the inventory will always be slightly higher.

items.statement: Future expansion beyond FY27 to reach 800-1000 crore revenue will be funded through internal accruals and equity
items.quote: This would be funded through internal accruals and equity.

items.statement: Cash balance of approximately Rs 30 crores held as cash and FDs, excluding treasury
items.quote: We also have a cash balance of approximately Rs. 30 crores. This does not include our treasury. This is purely cash and FD that is being held by us.

items.statement: Promoter group sold shares; 100% of proceeds went into the company to reduce debt and move toward zero-debt position.
items.quote: Whatever promoter group sale has happened, 100% of it has come into Kotyark Industries itself; I have not taken any money home.

items.statement: Promoter is reducing debt and taking the company toward a zero-debt position.
items.quote: No, I am reducing debt. I am taking the company towards a zero-debt position.
